gen-silkscreen-gf-shippori-antique-b1: Silkscreen spells everything out in lo-fi, pixel-sparse letters with space you can almost feel around each one, while Shippori Antique B1 stays open. Silkscreen is best at retro attitude; the plain sans is best at quiet legibility.
gen-silkscreen-gf-sn-pro: Every stroke of Silkscreen is the same thickness as bent wire, with no thick-to-thin shifts at all, and SN Pro stays open beside it. Retro, yet modern.
gen-silkscreen-gf-snippet: Playful and lo-fi, Silkscreen scatters its letters like spaghetti with air between each one. Snippet takes over below with a crescent-wrench c and a wire-bent look, friendly where the heading is quirky.
gen-silkscreen-gf-sour-gummy: Sour Gummy sets the modern tone with wide gaps. Silkscreen's thin plastic-tubing strokes bend in loops above it, so the sans-serif body feels like a tidy, grown-up neighbor to a retro toy.
gen-silkscreen-gf-source-sans-3: Retro pixels, then a modern exhale. Silkscreen's diagonals match its stems exactly, and Source Sans 3 opens the lower bowl of its a, so the pair hangs together through steadiness.
gen-silkscreen-gf-spinnaker: Lo-fi, spaced-out and retro. Silkscreen has no hairlines to match, so its stems all agree, and if the plain sans Spinnaker is sized up a little, its connected counters keep reading easily.
gen-silkscreen-gf-stick: Stick brings tubelike lines with exits wide enough to pass light through, and it is the quiet half of this pair. But if Silkscreen shrinks, its spaghetti spacing turns fussy, while a larger Stick would still hold.
gen-silkscreen-gf-suse: Silkscreen opens the pair as a lo-fi, retro display face with space around every letter you can nearly feel. SUSE, a sans-serif with rope-heavy curves and open bowls, would carry paragraphs comfortably.
gen-silkscreen-gf-suse-mono: SUSE Mono gives the sans-serif body open curves and extra space on both sides of every letter. And Silkscreen's constant, bent-wire strokes sit above it, so the page runs from retro to friendly.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tajawal: Clean and lo-fi at once, Silkscreen draws its letters with the weight of a drawn wire. Tajawal answers with a broad, open hook of a c, and that spare, tidy quality is what the two share.
